Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book:
- Policy statement: The 25 bp cut and “balanced risks” framing are mildly dovish, but ongoing QT and a hawkish dissent limit the dovish impulse.
- SLOOS: Credit remains restrictive where it matters (tight C&I, ongoing CRE tightening, softer demand for small/some middle‑market firms), justifying gradual easing; offsets include broadly unchanged residential/HELOC standards, some easing in multifamily at large banks, and stronger C&I demand at foreign banks; subprime consumer standards remain tighter.
- Beige Book cross‑check: District reports point to continued business activity with contacts expressing some optimism; non‑residential construction activity increased; employment growth persisted with firms still hiring even as some layoffs were reported; wages rose; prices and nonlabor input costs generally increased, though some districts saw declines in non‑labor costs; New York City CRE steadied with a pickup in office demand.
Net: Beige Book evidence of resilient activity and still‑present price pressures tempers the dovish read‑through from the cut and SLOOS headwinds. Overall tone remains mildly dovish but closer to neutral than a statement‑only/SLOOS read.
